paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: : labelformat=parens, labelsep=period
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between various metrics for AlphaEdit and DeltaEdit, specifically Efficacy top and noise E, across different x-axis values, with the x-axis labeled but without units, ranging from 0 to 3000 on a linear scale with tick labels at intervals of 500. The left y-axis, labeled "Efficacy top", spans from 86 to 100 on a linear scale with tick labels at intervals of 2, while the right y-axis, labeled "noise E", ranges from 2 to 12 on a linear scale with tick labels at intervals of 2. The plot displays four lines: AlphaEdit Efficacy top (red dashed line with square markers) starts at approximately 99 at x=0, decreases gradually to around 98.5 at x=1000, and then drops more sharply to about 86 at x=3000; DeltaEdit Efficacy top (blue dashed line with square markers) begins at around 99.5 at x=0, remains relatively stable until x=1500, and then declines to approximately 94 at x=3000; AlphaEdit noise E (red solid line with square markers) starts at around 3 at x=0, increases steadily to about 12 at x=3000; DeltaEdit noise E (blue solid line with square markers) follows a similar trend to AlphaEdit noise E, starting at approximately 3 at x=0 and rising to around 11.5 at x=3000.
